ai_text_by_case.us-v-hoskins: Restrictions on Use of AI to Process Materials. No person or entity authorized to have access to Materials under the terms of this Order shall input, transmit, upload, process, generate output from, or otherwise expose any Materials received pursuant to this order to any artificial intelligence ("AI") tool without prior written notice to, and corresponding receipt of acknowledgement from, the government. "AI tool" means any automated system that uses statistical modeling, machine learning, or similar techniques to process inputs and generate outputs, recommendations, or predictions, including but not limited to large language models, generative AI services, or AI-assisted software tools, whether cloud-based or otherwise. When providing written notice for the otherwise prohibited use of an AI tool, defense counsel must specifically identify and describe any AI tool to be used and certify that it does not (i) retain or use any Materials for model training, nor (ii) expose any Materials to third parties not authorized under this order to receive such materials. In addition, defense counsel must certify that: (i) defense counsel has implemented reasonable measures to ensure that any AI tool used will maintain the confidentiality of any Materials, and (ii) defense counsel will ensure the deletion of all Materials from the tool at the conclusion of this case. Defense counsel will be responsible for destroying such information at that time. Under no circumstances will any member of the defense team submit Materials to a publicly accessible AI system that retains and uses submitted data to train models. Such AI tools pose unique risks to the security and integrity of Materials, given the practical inability to claw back or delete data once it has been incorporated into a model.

ai_text_by_case.skaf-v-google: Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools and Large Language Models. Protected Material, and all information derived therefrom, shall not be inputted, uploaded, or submitted to any open, publicly accessible or freely available consumer-grade Large Language Model ("LLM") or Artificial Intelligence ("AI") tool (collectively, "AI Tools"). Protected Material may only be inputted, uploaded, or submitted to an AI Tool that is enterprise-grade and maintains confidential information using industry standard data security safeguards ("Confidential AI Tool") after the Receiving Party first ensures that its contract with the AI Provider of the Confidential AI Tool: (1) Prohibits the AI Provider from storing or using inputs to train, refine, or improve its model; (2) Prohibits the AI Provider from disclosing inputs, metadata, and any information generated by the Confidential AI Tool to any third party, including integrated third party tools, except where such disclosure is essential to facilitating delivery of the service, in which case that third party shall be bound by obligations no less protective than those required by this Order; and (3) Permits the Receiving Party to remove or delete the Protected Material, and any information generated by the Confidential AI Tool upon request. A Receiving Party intending to use a Confidential AI Tool that it contends meets these requirements must retain written documentation of these contractual protections. In addition, the Protected Material, and any information generated by the Confidential AI Tool, including residual information stored in the Confidential AI Tool as a result of the submission of the Protected Material, must be deleted from the Confidential AI Tool at the close of the litigation, and in accordance with the Final Disposition section below. Any inputs, outputs, models, or other artifacts (e.g., embeddings, indexes, or logs) used in or created by a Confidential AI Tool that are derived from or contain Protected Material shall be subject to Section 7.1 and shall not be used for any purpose other than prosecuting or defending this litigation. For the avoidance of doubt, submitting Protected Material, or excerpts therefrom, to any AI Tool that does not meet the requirements of this section is considered unauthorized disclosure to a third party under Section 10 of this Order. Nothing in this provision shall alter the obligations set forth in Section 1 ("Purposes and Limitations") and Section 12.9 ("Data Security") of this Order.

ai_text_by_case.doe-v-google: Any person in possession of Protected Material will maintain appropriate administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards ("Safeguards") that protect the security and privacy of Protected Material, including restrictions regarding the disclosure or use of Protected Material in any large language models or any artificial intelligence services. The Safeguards will meet relevant industry standards and limit the collection, storage, disclosure, use of, or access to Protected Material solely to personnel and purposes authorized by this Order. As part of these Safeguards, each person will use a secure transfer method for all transfers or communication of Protected Material, and take reasonable measures to password protect and encrypt Protected Material. Each person will ensure that anyone acting on that person's behalf is subject to the Safeguards or otherwise provides equivalent or greater protections for the security and privacy of Protected Material. Such restrictions shall, at a minimum, prohibit the disclosure or use of Protected Material in any large language models or artificial intelligence services that are accessible to the public or will capture entered data in order to train what is accessible by the public.
ai_text_by_case.rapacon-v-abbott: "CONFIDENTIAL" Information or Items shall not be submitted to any Open Generative AI tool (e.g., Chat GPT) or any substantially similar tool that is available to the public. Providing "CONFIDENTIAL" Information or Items to an Open Generative AI tool is considered disclosure to a third party. For purposes of this Protective Order, "Open Generative AI tool" means an artificial intelligence system that may be accessed by the public, or that allows for the underlying code and materials to be accessed by the public. The Parties may only submit "CONFIDENTIAL" Information or Items to a Permitted Generative AI Tool. For purposes of this Protective Order, a "Permitted Generative AI Tool" includes the use of enterprise AI tools that: (i) restrict access to authorized users; (ii) do not use customer data to train, refine, fine-tune, or improve publicly available models; (iii) provide reasonable retention and deletion controls; and (iv) maintain commercially reasonable security and confidentiality protections. ai_text_by_case.zl-technologies-v-kldiscovery: (a) Scope: To protect the confidentiality and security of all information disclosed or produced in this proceeding ("Discovery Information"), any Party receiving Discovery Information from another Party ("Receiving Party") shall comply with the following requirements governing the use of artificial intelligence ("AI") tools with such information. (b) Permitted AI Use: A Receiving Party may use AI tools to process Discovery Information solely for purposes of this proceeding, provided that the AI tool and its use collectively satisfy all of the following requirements: i. Restricted, Enterprise Environment: The AI tool is used pursuant to a written enterprise or professional agreement and is deployed within a secure, access-controlled environment. ii. No Model Training or External Use: Discovery Information is not used to train, fine-tune, improve, develop, benchmark, or otherwise contribute to any AI model or service accessible outside the Receiving Party's environment, except to the limited extent necessary to provide the requested functionality for this proceeding. iii. Data Retention and Deletion: Within 30 days after final disposition of this action, Discovery Information retained by the AI tool shall be destroyed or caused to be destroyed to the extent reasonably possible. iv. Security Safeguards: The AI tool is subject to technical and contractual safeguards reasonably designed to protect Discovery Information against unauthorized access, use, or disclosure, including encryption in transit and at rest and appropriate access controls. (c) No Backdoor Access: Nothing in Section 23 permits a Party, Agent, Expert, or other person that is not able to access Confidential Discovery Information or Highly Confidential - Attorneys' Eyes Only Information under this Order to use AI tools to query, analyze, search or otherwise process such information. ai_text_by_case.stt-webos-v-bytedance: Artificial Intelligence Use. The Parties agree that any documents, electronically stored information ("ESI"), or other materials produced or exchanged in the course of this Action, including but not limited to those designated as "CONFIDENTIAL," "HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEYS' EYES ONLY," or "HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL - SOURCE CODE" under this Order, shall not be used, in whole or in part, for prompts (inputs), completions (outputs), or embeddings that are used to train, improve, re-train, or otherwise develop any artificial intelligence, foundation model, or large language model (collectively "AI Models"). This prohibition applies regardless of whether the AI Models are proprietary, open-source, or provided by a third party, and regardless of whether the use is for commercial, research, or any other purpose. The Parties further agree to take reasonable steps to ensure that their employees, counsel, agents, consultants, contractors, and any other persons or entities who may have access to such materials comply with this prohibition. Any violation of this provision may be addressed by the Court through appropriate remedies, including but not limited to sanctions.
ai_text_by_case.corent-v-aws: No party, and no person or entity authorized to receive materials under this Order, may input, upload, submit, or otherwise provide any Discovery Material-whether or not designated as Protected Information-into any modern artificial intelligence platform, including any generative, analytical, or large language model-based tool ("AI Tool"), unless all requirements of Section 12.1 and Section 12.2 are satisfied. 12.1 A party or person subject to this Order may use an AI Tool with Discovery Material only if the AI Tool is provided on an enterprise or commercial tier subscription and the Receiving Party has not configured the AI Tool to: a) retain or store inputs (including prompts, documents, and metadata) for use beyond the session necessary to deliver the requested service, except as provided in Section 12.7.2, For clarity, this requirement does not prohibit the use of AI Tools that maintain a history of a user's prompts and/or sessions, provided that any prompts containing Protected Information shall not be disclosed to any person not authorized to receive Protected Information under this Order; b) use, incorporate, or reference inputs to train, fine-tune, retrain, or otherwise improve any AI model or system, whether that of the vendor or any third party, except as provided in Section 12.7.2, For clarity, this requirement does not prohibit the use of AI tools that incorporate or reference a user's past prompts to optimize responses to subsequent prompts by the same user, provided that such AI tools (1) do not use, reference, or incorporate prompts or other inputs received from one user to respond to prompts from any other user; and (2) otherwise comply with all of the requirements in Section 12; c) disclose inputs to any third party, except where strictly essential to facilitate delivery of the service; any such third party must be bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those required by this Order; d) allow any human employee, contractor, or reviewer of the AI vendor to read, access, or review input content for any purpose other than immediate technical support explicitly requested by the party; and e) make inputs or retained outputs accessible to any person not authorized to receive Protected Information under this Order. 12.2 In addition to the requirements of Section 12.1, a party or person may use an AI Tool with Discovery Material only if the AI vendor is contractually obligated to afford the Receiving Party the right to remove or delete all Discovery Material and AI-generated outputs from the vendor's systems upon request, and in any event no later than sixty (60) days following the entry of a final non-appealable judgment or order, or the complete settlement of all claims asserted against all parties in this action (the "Conclusion of This Action"). The Receiving Party shall: (a) within fourteen (14) days following the Conclusion of This Action, take all reasonable steps necessary to ensure deletion of all Protected Material uploaded and/or output by AI tools during this action. The Receiving Party may meet this requirement by submitting a deletion request to the vendor if the vendor accepts deletion requests during the term of its vendor agreement with the Receiving Party; or, if the AI vendor does not accept such requests, by manually deleting all uploaded information over the AI tool's user interface; and (b) within sixty (60) days following the Conclusion of This Action, provide the Producing Party with written certification and documentation demonstrating that the Receiving Party took all reasonable steps necessary to delete all Discovery Material uploaded to AI tools using the procedures and means provided by the vendor(s), as applicable. 12.3 Any party intending to use an AI Tool with Discovery Material must, prior to such use: a) retain written documentation (including the vendor's data processing agreement, terms of service, or equivalent contractual instrument) demonstrating that the vendor's commitments satisfy Sections 12.1 and 12.2; and b) make such documentation available to the Producing Party within five (5) business days of a written request. 12.4 A party that intends to use an AI Tool with Discovery Material produced by the other party must provide written notice to the Producing Party at least seven (7) business days before first use, except with respect to AI Tools pre-approved under Section 12.6. Such notice shall identify: a) the name, version, and operator of the AI Tool; b) the categories of Discovery Material the Receiving Party intends to process; and c) a representation that Sections 12.1 and 12.2 are satisfied, accompanied by the documentation required by Section 12.3(a). The Producing Party shall have five (5) business days to object in writing, stating with particularity the basis for objection. If a timely objection is served, the parties shall meet and confer within three (3) business days. If the dispute is not resolved, the Receiving Party may not proceed with such AI Tool use until the Court resolves the dispute pursuant to Local Rule 37-1 et seq. and Section 3 of Judge McCormick's Procedures. 12.5 Notwithstanding any other provision of this Section 12, no party may use any AI Tool, regardless of vendor contractual protections, to review, analyze, summarize, or otherwise process any Discovery Material designated as HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL-SOURCE CODE. This prohibition is absolute and applies whether such Source Code material is accessed on the Source Code Computer, in printed form, in electronic excerpts, or in any other form or medium. 12.6 The parties agree that the following AI Tools, when used at the enterprise or commercial tier identified below and subject to the configuration requirements in this subsection, satisfy the requirements of Sections 12.1 and 12.2 based on each vendor's published enterprise terms of service, data processing addendum, and security certifications as of the Effective Date of this Order. Use of any AI Tool pre-approved under this Section 12.6 shall not require the pre-use notice otherwise required under Section 12.4. a) Microsoft Copilot, including Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Cowork, when deployed within a Microsoft 365 Enterprise or Business tenant governed by Microsoft's enterprise Data Protection Addendum (and not the free or consumer-facing Copilot product available at copilot.microsoft.com), satisfies the requirements of Sections 12.1 and 12.2, provided that: (i) the Receiving Party's tenant is configured to disable any consumer connectors or web-grounding features that would route Discovery Material outside the enterprise data-processing boundary; and (ii) the Receiving Party has not enabled any consumer-tier or non-Enterprise Copilot product for use with Discovery Material. b) Lexis+ AI (LexisNexis), at the firm's standard commercial or enterprise subscription tier, satisfies the requirements of Sections 12.1 and 12.2, provided that: (i) the Receiving Party's account is configured under LexisNexis's then-current commercial terms and its published zero-training and zero-retention commitments applicable to user-submitted content; and (ii) the Receiving Party has not enabled any consumer or free-tier LexisNexis AI product for use with Discovery Material. c) Westlaw AI and CoCounsel (Thomson Reuters), at the firm's standard commercial or enterprise subscription tier, satisfy the requirements of Sections 12.1 and 12.2, provided that: (i) the Receiving Party's account is governed by Thomson Reuters's then-current commercial terms, including its non-retention API arrangements with underlying model providers and its contractual prohibition on third-party model providers retaining or training on customer data; and (ii) the Receiving Party has not enabled any consumer or free-tier Westlaw AI or CoCounsel product for use with Discovery Material. d) Patlytics (patlytics.ai), at the firm's standard commercial or enterprise subscription tier, satisfies the requirements of Sections 12.1 and 12.2, provided that: (i) the Receiving Party's account is configured under Patlytics's then-current customer terms, including its published non-training commitment and its non-retention agreements with underlying third-party AI services; ai_text_by_case.fischman-v-epic: Use of Protected Material with Artificial Intelligence Platforms 26. The following provisions govern the use of Protected Material in and with artificial - intelligence platforms. Case 3:26-cv-00770-D Document 58 Filed 10/23/26 Page 16 of 25 PageID 1029 27. No person subject to this Protective Order may input, upload, submit, or otherwise transfer any Protected Material into any artificial -intelligence platform, including any generative, analytical, or large-language-model-based tool ("AI Platform"), unless the provider of the AI Platform is contractually prohibited from (i) storing or using the inputs to train or improve any model, and (ii) disclosing the inputs to any third party except to the limited extent essential to deliver the requested service, and the provider contractually affords the ability to require deletion o f all such inputs. This restriction applies regardless of whether the Protected Material has been anonymized, redacted, or summarized. As a practical matter, this provision prohibits entering Protected Material into the standard consumer or other publicly accessible versions of widely available generative artificial - intelligence services-such as, but not limited to, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot-that retain user inputs or use them to train or improve their models. This provision does not prohibit the use of enterprise versions of generative artificial-intelligence services that comply with the restrictions in this section. 28. Nothing in this provision restricts any Party from using AI Platforms for any purpose that does not involve inputting another Party's Protected Material, or from using an AI Platform that satisfies the requirements of Paragraph 27. This provision shall not be construed to limit any Party's use of artificial intelligence for legal research, drafting, organization, or other litigation tasks that do not entail the input of Protected Material. 29. To the extent a Party is unsure whether a specific AI Platform satisfies Paragraph 27, the Party agrees that, prior to entering any Protected Material into the AI Platform, it will confer with the Designating Party(ies). If such parties are unable to agree on whether the AI Platform at issue satisfies Paragraph 27, the party opposed to its use may submit an appropriate motion to the Court. Until either the parties come to an agreement or the Court makes a determination, whichever is earlier, no Protected Material may be entered into the AI Platform at issue. Case 3:26-cv-00770-D Document 58 Filed 10/23/26 Page 17 of 25 PageID 1030 30. Any person who uses Protected Material as an input into an AI Platform in reliance on Paragraph 27 shall retain written documentation of the contractual protections relied upon, and shall, upon request by the D esignating Party, identify the AI Platform used and produce that documentation. This paragraph does not require the disclosure of any AI Platform used solely for purposes permitted by Paragraph 28. 31. Nothing in this Protective Order shall be interpreted as requiring a self -represented party to purchase, subscribe to, or maintain any particular software, platform, or technology - including any enterprise AI platform-in order to participate in discovery.
ai_text_by_case.james-v-cerebras: 13.4 Large Language Models / Generative AI Tools. All Parties shall take commercially reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized access to any Protected Material, including when using generative AI tools or large language models ("LLMs"). Without notifying and obtaining permission from the Producing Party, individuals or entities with access to Protected Material under this Order must not use Protected Material in AI tools or similar applications (e.g., OpenAI GPT, ChatGPT, Google Bard, Meta LLAMA) without taking commercially reasonable efforts to ensure such tools (a) do not incorporate inputs into model weights, or otherwise train on Protected Material, and (b) adhere to industry standard cybersecurity practices and provide sufficient administrative controls to prevent unauthorized access. For the avoidance of doubt, the parties' enterprise ChatGPT and Harvey accounts satisfy the foregoing requirements.
